inputs.name: events per haploid genome per generation
inputs.cite: evo009@L37 (Hancock, relayed); B5c (76.8 = 6.4e9 x 1.2e-8; 152/2 = 76 events incl. SVs)

day.reading: a total mutation rate must be compared with a total divergence, not the SNV fraction
day.holds: the units are mixed: the rate counts events of every type, the 35M counts SNVs only; Duffy (evo008@L83) was right to flag it

critic.reading: the fixation equation does not distinguish mutation types; the swap of rate is a point against Hancock's whiteboard, not against neutral theory
critic.holds: in events the mismatch is 1.11-1.14x (SNVs are 87.5-89.7% of events); the 98.91% is a share of genome sites, not of the mutations, so it overstates the mismatch about 80-fold

notes: Not like for like, as Day and Duffy say; the matching comparator for an all-events rate is all events (40M CSAC, 42.10M GAP-07b), not SNVs and not base pairs. The ratio the post draws (98.91% omitted) is 100 - 1.09, where 1.09% = 35e6/3.2e9 is the SNV share of genome sites; read as a share of the divergence it would be 12.5% (events) or 91.2% (Day's bp), and bp cannot be set against an event rate (A3x). The relay's 'u = (3e9)*(76.8)' is a slip for 76.8/3e9. 76.8 is numerically the diploid SNV product 6.4e9 x 1.2e-8 (B5c), while the post calls it a haploid all-events rate (152/2 = 76); which one Hancock meant is not settled here. Duffy's 169,344 is M-109.
